# Slide 20

**Spurious Correlations**

**(Image Description):**

This slide presents a collection of three sets of line graphs, each exploring potential correlations between seemingly unrelated variables.  The graphs are arranged in a grid-like format, with each set of graphs positioned in a separate section of the slide.

* **Top Left (Total revenue generated by arcades vs. Computer science doctorates awarded):**  A line graph displays the total revenue generated by arcades in the US (red line) and the number of computer science doctorates awarded in the US (black line) over time (approximately 2000-2008).  The x-axis represents the year, and the y-axis represents the revenue (in billions of dollars) and the number of doctorates.  The graph visually shows the correlation between the two variables.  The correlation is noted as 98.51% (-0.985065).  The purpose of this graph is to illustrate a potential spurious correlation between arcade revenue and computer science doctorates.

* **Top Right (Worldwide non-commercial space launches vs. Sociology doctorates awarded):** A line graph displays the number of worldwide non-commercial space launches (red line) and the number of sociology doctorates awarded in the US (black line) over time (approximately 1990-2008).  The x-axis represents the year, and the y-axis represents the number of launches and the number of doctorates.  The graph visually shows the correlation between the two variables.  The correlation is noted as 78.92% (-0.78915).  The purpose of this graph is to illustrate a potential spurious correlation between space launches and sociology doctorates.

* **Bottom (Per capita consumption of mozzarella cheese vs. Civil engineering doctorates awarded):** A line graph displays the per capita consumption of mozzarella cheese (red line) and the number of civil engineering doctorates awarded in the US (black line) over time (approximately 2000-2013).  The x-axis represents the year, and the y-axis represents the per capita consumption of mozzarella cheese and the number of doctorates.  The graph visually shows the correlation between the two variables.  The correlation is noted as 85.95% (r=0.958648).  The purpose of this graph is to illustrate a potential spurious correlation between mozzarella cheese consumption and civil engineering doctorates.


**Overall Context (Intro to Data Science):**

This slide, in the context of an Intro to Data Science lecture, demonstrates the concept of spurious correlations.  It visually presents three examples of seemingly correlated variables (arcade revenue and computer science degrees, space launches and sociology degrees, and mozzarella consumption and civil engineering degrees) that likely have no causal relationship.  The slide is intended to highlight the importance of critical thinking and caution when interpreting correlations in data analysis.  The graphs are designed to show how seemingly strong correlations can be coincidental and not indicative of a true relationship.  The inclusion of the correlation percentages emphasizes the strength of the apparent relationship, but also underscores the need for further investigation to determine if a true relationship exists.  The source is noted as https://www.tylervigen.com/spurious-correlations.
